sections.h2: City or county: check this first
sections.html:
Charlottesville is an independent city in central Virginia, and it is the county seat of Albemarle County, which surrounds it on all sides. The two are separate governments. The 2020 census counted 46,553 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 44,388. The wider metro area, which takes in Albemarle, Fluvanna, Greene and Nelson counties, has about 221,524 people.

Before you plan a sale, confirm which side of the line your parcel is on. A house with a Charlottesville mailing address may sit in Albemarle County, and the tax office, permit office and zoning rules change with the line. Most of the University of Virginia's grounds, for example, are legally in the county even though they feel like part of the city. Your tax bill shows who taxes the parcel, and that is the office you call about anything owed.

The town dates to 1762 and grew up along a trade route that is today's U.S. 250, later becoming a rail hub. Court Square is the original center, and the Downtown Mall beside it is one of the longest outdoor pedestrian malls in the country. A house near that old core and a house in a later subdivision have very different repair needs: older homes tend to bring older wiring, plumbing and roofs, while newer ones bring different questions about systems and warranties.

When someone contacts us, we ask for the build year first because it tells us what to look for during a walkthrough. If you have permits or receipts for past work, gather them. They help a buyer see what has already been done and can support a firmer offer.

The University of Virginia and its health system anchor the local job base, joined by city government, the schools and research or finance institutions. More than 20,000 students come to the city during the academic year, which affects rental demand near campus. Only about 18 percent of the people employed in Charlottesville live in the city. About 82 percent commute in, and 42 percent of those commuters come from Albemarle County, while 11,497 city residents commute out for work.

In plain terms, many people with jobs here live in the county, so a city seller competes with county houses for the same buyers. Two hospitals serve the area, University of Virginia Hospital and Martha Jefferson Hospital, and Piedmont Virginia Community College adds a steady stream of renters and first-time buyers.

sections.h2: Weather and what to check on the house
sections.html:
Summers are hot and humid, winters are cool, and rain falls in every month. The high passes 90 degrees on roughly 34 days a year, and snowfall averages 17 inches a season but rarely stays long. The wettest stretch is May through September, so air conditioning, attic ventilation and gutters all get a workout.

  • Test the air conditioning and keep any service record to show a buyer.
  • Inspect the attic and the roof before listing.
  • Look at the ground around the foundation for erosion or pooling after storms.
  • Check the crawl space for moisture.

Virginia's seller disclosure form tells buyers that the owner makes no statement about special flood hazard areas, dam break inundation zones, radon zones or marine clay soils. Buyers can research those on their own, and a note from you about any past water problem builds trust.

Interstate 64 and U.S. 29 are the main highways, with U.S. 250 and Virginia Route 20 also serving the city. Charlottesville Area Transit runs city buses, JAUNT operates paratransit vans, and University Transit Service covers the area around the university. The Charlottesville-Albemarle Airport handles commercial flights, and the Amtrak station sees the Cardinal three times a week plus daily Crescent and Northeast Regional trains.

A house within walking distance of the Downtown Mall or a bus corridor appeals to renters and downsizers. A house outside the core suits buyers who drive. We weigh both when we price a cash offer.

Charlottesville City Schools run six elementary schools, Walker Upper Elementary School, Buford Middle School and Charlottesville High School. Albemarle County Public Schools serve the surrounding county. If you are unsure whether your house is in the city or the county, the school system is one more clue, since some private schools with Charlottesville postal addresses are actually in the county. Call the city's planning and building offices and the treasurer to confirm any local requirement before you list, rent or renovate.

sections.h2: What Virginia sellers pay and sign
sections.html:
Virginia imposes a grantor's tax on the seller, set at 50 cents for each $500 of the price. The buyer and seller can agree in the contract to shift it. The tax is shared between the state and the locality, and the circuit court clerk will not record the deed until it is paid. The statute is Virginia Code 58.1-802.

You must also hand the buyer the Real Estate Board's residential property disclosure statement. The form states that the owner makes no representations on topics such as historic district rules, lot lines, adjacent parcels, flood hazards, easements, lead plumbing, drywall and the condition of any dam. Starting January 1, 2027, the statute adds an item about use-value assessment and roll-back taxes. The text is at Virginia Code 55.1-703.

Unpaid real estate tax is a lien that outranks other liens, and the closing agent pays it from the seller's proceeds. The seller's share of the current year's tax is divided by contract, so the sales agreement should say who covers which days. The lien rule is at Virginia Code 58.1-3340.

  • Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure before closing day.
  • Have the title company search for liens and judgments.
  • Write down in the contract who pays the grantor's tax and recording costs.

A cash sale means the buyer does not need a mortgage, so the deal depends less on lender timing, appraisals and loan approvals. The steps are simple:

  1. You contact us with the address and a few details.
  2. We review the house and make a written offer.
  3. If you accept, a title company handles the deed, payoffs and the closing paperwork.
  4. You pick a closing date that fits your move.

Owners in the city sometimes ask about a house they inherited, a rental that needs work, or a house they must leave quickly for a job change. We buy as-is, so you do not have to clean out the house or make repairs first. If the offer does not suit you, you owe us nothing and you can list with an agent instead.

This is general information about Charlottesville, not legal or tax advice. Check specifics with an attorney or the local government.

faqs.a: No. Charlottesville is an independent city and the county seat of Albemarle County, but the two are separate governments. Your tax bill and address records show which one covers your parcel.

faqs.q: How many people live in Charlottesville?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 46,553 people, and the 2025 estimate is 44,388.

faqs.q: What does Virginia charge a seller when a deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Under Virginia Code 58.1-802 the grantor pays 50 cents for each $500 of the sale price, unless the contract moves some or all of it to the buyer. The clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Charlottesville without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Virginia's disclosure form is built around the buyer doing their own due diligence, so you can sell as-is. You still give the buyer the Real Estate Board's disclosure statement.

faqs.q: Which airport and train station serve Charlottesville?
faqs.a: Charlottesville-Albemarle Airport handles commercial flights, and the Amtrak station is served by the Cardinal, Crescent and select Northeast Regional trains.
